cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers both T2 and T3 at once; T8 picks up T7's branches directly.
cells.limitation: T9 jumps back to T4's finitude point instead of answering T8's tests.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces thing/friend/audience distinction; T7, T8 and Section E build on it.
cells.limitation: T8 adds practical tests rather than a new conceptual distinction.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T3 vs T2: different drummer versus fear or contrarian borrowed desire.
cells.limitation: T7 names freedom versus belonging, then nobody examines it.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T5 narrows Thoreau after T4; T11 narrows Girard after T10; disputes kept in Section D.
cells.limitation: T10 agrees with T9 without noting T4 already said drifting is a choice.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D: feeling behind and not wanting milestones can both be true.
cells.limitation: Whether waiting is wise stays restated in Section D rather than sharpened.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 grants the drummer reading could be true, then shows it is indistinguishable from fear.
cells.limitation: T9 charges Burkeman with excusing drift, which T4 already disowned.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T10 names assumption borrowed equals fake; T11 answers with a narrowed test.
cells.limitation: T9's objection targets a position nobody held after T4.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T2 Walden drummer quote is in a pd=true turn and matches the text.
cells.limitation: T4 asserts flatly there is no track; Section E claims social pressure may simply fade.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10 marks its own extension: I'd go further than the book here.
cells.limitation: T1 bets the feeling is not about the things before any evidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T11 concedes borrowed does not mean false and states a narrower claim.
cells.limitation: T10 concedes T9's charge rather than noting T4 already granted it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the unknown: wanting, missing friends, or comparison.
cells.limitation: T1 says you don't want them; user said not sure.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T6 turns friends' weddings and houses into a test of what stings.
cells.limitation: Little user detail exists; friendship closeness used only in T7-T8.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T7: ranking freedom and belonging is your call.
cells.limitation: User's own priorities never probed beyond the T6 sting question.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9: not being sure can last forever while real doors close.
cells.limitation: Age, partner, money never raised; T9's closing doors stay abstract.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T6 and Section E branch thing/friend/audience, stating what each implies.
cells.limitation: Whether user is partnered or can afford a home never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 offers three motives as alternatives with a question the user can answer.
cells.limitation: T1 leans toward one motive with I'd bet before alternatives appear.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 exposes the race assumption; T10 exposes borrowed equals fake.
cells.limitation: Assumption that milestones measure being on time is not probed directly.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T7: freedom and belonging may be pulling against each other.
cells.limitation: The freedom-belonging conflict gets one sentence in T7 and is dropped.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T3: different drummer and fear of the dance floor look identical.
cells.limitation: Fear of losing friends raised in T6 is not explored as fear.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T11 test: would you want it if no one could see it.
cells.limitation: T1 frames the doubt as puzzling before inviting the user's reading.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E: small trials, reinvest in friendships, or deliberate waiting.
cells.limitation: What is being decided is never stated; options emerge only as branches.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4: every path costs you the others, and drifting is a choice.
cells.limitation: Costs of the T8 trials and of deliberate waiting go unstated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: what stings decides between trials, friendship, or waiting.
cells.limitation: Section E's next month and T7's this month are not drawn from user facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section E's fourth branch handles not being able to tell which it is.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not explicitly set aside from the main one.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T8: open house, ask a married friend, or just call the friend.
cells.limitation: T8's host a dinner is unclear about what it would test.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T4: behind implies one lane and a finish line.
cells.limitation: T1 desire spreads through models is compressed jargon without gloss.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 You're both assuming clearly points at T2 and T3.
cells.limitation: T9 and T10 address minds by author names, not Section B titles.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: 11 turns, all within word range; short turns keep momentum.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Suspicion, testing and finitude stay distinct; T5 states its shift explicitly.
cells.limitation: Experimenter's T8 voice is plain advice, little Thoreau texture.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section D recap restates the T6 question as the reflection prompt.
cells.limitation: Section E largely repeats T7-T8 branches.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T3 challenge that refusal may be borrowed creates real tension.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; T9's closing doors never made concrete.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T11 Detective concedes, citing T10's argument that people learn to love things.
cells.limitation: T5's narrowing is a mild shift, not a surprise.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T1 Detective: your friends are broadcasting.
cells.limitation: Experimenter and Realist lose personality in T7-T8.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: different drummer versus afraid of the dance floor.
cells.limitation: T7-T8 are serviceable lists without memorable lines.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T9's sharp turn against the Realist after practical T8 changes rhythm.
cells.limitation: Emotional register stays even; little movement after T6.

strengths: T6 introduces the thing/friend/audience distinction that T7, T8 and Section E build into conditional branches.
Caused revisions: T5 Experimenter narrows after T4; T11 Detective concedes after T10's borrowed-is-not-fake argument.
T3's different drummer versus fear of the dance floor sharpens the central ambiguity vividly.
weaknesses: Practical constraints (age, partner, money) never raised; T9's closing doors stay abstract.
T7 Finitude Realist names freedom versus belonging, then no mind examines it.
T9 Desire Detective attacks a drift excuse the Finitude Realist already disowned in T4.

symptoms.observed: Stakes and constraints stay abstract; no question about partner, finances or timing.
symptoms.evidence: Not being sure can last forever, and meanwhile real doors close.

symptoms.observed: Values conflict named in one sentence, never examined by any mind.
symptoms.evidence: Freedom and belonging may be pulling against each other

symptoms.observed: T9 attacks a view the Realist already rejected in T4.
symptoms.evidence: Burkeman, your finitude talk can become a permanent excuse.

symptoms.observed: Opening restates the user's doubt as a settled non-want.
symptoms.evidence: you don't want the house or the wedding, yet you feel behind

symptoms.observed: Time frame for action not derived from the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: you can act on it this month

findings.description: Walden drummer quotation in a pd=true turn; matches the text from memory, no evidence attached.
Claims social pressure may fade without change; offered without support or condition.

rubric_fit_notes: Self-reflection labelled decision: the user poses no explicit choice, so C5 cells were read as the basis for responding to the feeling.
question_type_note: Read as decision per the label, with options taken as ways to respond to feeling behind rather than whether to buy or marry.
